sources.material_consulted: Section 1, printed pages 455-456, including the total-variance identity and the conditional-expectation computation/cost caveat; these two pages visually inspected as well as text read
sources.supports: Conditional Monte Carlo is established; projection preserves expectation and lowers observation variance. Computability and per-replication work matter for efficiency.

sources.title: Control Variate Remedies
sources.consulted_version: Final journal scan hosted on the author's Northwestern University page
sources.material_consulted: Sections 1-2, printed pages 975-977, and Section 6, pages 979-980. Printed pages 975, 976 and 979 visually inspected; selected surrounding text read.
sources.supports: Known-mean linear controls, population coefficients and distinctions between finite-sample and asymptotic inference. Section 6 explains the independent preliminary-sample remedy for coefficient-induced bias.
sources.limitations: Published exact small-sample variance formula in Section 6 imposes joint normality. The capped-lognormal payoff/control pair is not jointly normal; no transfer of that formula or exact Student coverage is justified.

interpretation: These are established classical methods. The project-specific contribution is a proved, reproducible capped-GBM comparison and a demonstration of when failing to project the control adds variance. No theoretical priority, practical quantum advantage or finite-pilot dominance is claimed.
